requirements.summary: ufw explicitly allows 22/tcp (v4+v6), confirmed active both pre-reboot (cmd-80678b7e98ec4d59) and post-reboot (cmd-e40dab086ac347a0); sshd remained active throughout.
ufw explicitly allows 8080/tcp (v4+v6), confirmed active both pre- and post-reboot alongside the SSH rule.

requirements.requirement: Unrelated inbound connections are rejected by default
requirements.summary: ufw default incoming policy set to reject and confirmed active; underlying iptables INPUT chain policy is DROP and routes through the ufw-reject-input chain, matching the required behavior for any port other than 22/8080.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent across restart
requirements.summary: Full bounded restart transition observed: pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 8336c3a1..., ufw active with correct rules, sshd active) via cmd-80678b7e98ec4d59; reboot acknowledged via cmd-02fea6dc1a534480; node unreachable mid-reboot (cmd-4e705d05d64748b8, refused) then returned with a new boot_id f333f02f... (cmd-d3297a622a324a15); post-restart state confirms ufw automatically active again with identical allow rules for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, default reject incoming, ufw service enabled/active, and sshd active (cmd-e40dab086ac347a0). This satisfies the required pre-state/disruption/recovery evidence chain for a persistence claim.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — SSH allowed, TCP 8080 allowed, unrelated inbound rejected by default, and persistence across restart — are directly and coherently satisfied. The executor performed a genuine bounded reboot with pre/post boot-identity and rule-state comparison, which fully substantiates the persistence claim rather than relying on configuration alone. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were identified.
limitations: Rejection behavior for unrelated ports is verified via configuration (ufw default reject, iptables DROP policy) rather than an actual external connection attempt to a blocked port, though this is standard and sufficient evidence for a non-availability requirement.
Listening-socket and package-health snapshots returned empty/minimal output in both before and after captures, limiting their diagnostic value beyond confirming no failed services.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 11 executor commands chronologically. State-changing commands were: OS/tool inspection (read-only), ufw default-policy and allow-rule changes (cmd-545f85eb407b40ec, cmd-57b71f3cf2e145f7) directly implementing the required rules, ufw enable (cmd-ba9ded8b76714ea2) required for persistence, and a single reboot (cmd-02fea6dc1a534480) used specifically to produce the required restart-persistence evidence. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; the intermediate 'deny' policy was immediately tightened to 'reject' as part of a coherent, minimal rule-build sequence rather than an abandoned experiment. Temp-file and package-health differences between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots are attributable to the reboot itself (systemd-private dirs regenerated) rather than executor residue, and no failed services or listening-socket anomalies appear post-executor.
